title: Tipping in Türkiye 2026: Restaurants, Guides, Drivers & Hotels
seoTitle: Tipping in Türkiye 2026: Restaurants, Guides & Hotels
metaDescription: Exact 2026 tipping norms in Türkiye for restaurants, meyhanes, private guides, drivers, hamams, and hotels—plus the 2026 service charge ban.
quickAnswer: Tipping (bahşiş) in Türkiye is customary for good service but never mandatory. Leave 10% in cash Turkish lira at sit-down restaurants and meyhanes, tip private guides €20–€40 per day per group (and drivers roughly half), and give hamam attendants 10%–20%. Since January 30, 2026, mandatory restaurant service and cover charges are banned nationwide.
category: Practical Travel Logistics, Money, Visas & Transport

body.text: How much should you tip at restaurants, cafes and meyhanes?

At sit-down restaurants and traditional meyhanes, 10% in cash Turkish lira is the standard thank-you for attentive service, with 5%–10% normal at neighborhood spots and 10%–15% at fine-dining rooms. At casual cafés, bakeries, and lokanta steam-table canteens, simply round up the bill or drop spare change into the counter tip box (bahşiş kutusu).

Pay your meal by credit card if you prefer, but leave the tip separately in cash. Most Turkish card terminals lack a dedicated tip prompt, and as [Hürriyet Daily News reported](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiye-moves-to-ban-mandatory-extra-charges-at-cafes-restaurants-216282), card-processed tips are often recorded as business revenue and taxed heavily before reaching staff. Leaving clean lira notes inside the bill folder ensures the server and kitchen pool actually receive your gratuity.

body.text: What is the standard daily tip for private guides and drivers?

For a full-day private tour in 2026, published local guidance places a fair tip at €20–€40 per day for your licensed guide and €10–€20 per day for your dedicated driver, calculated per group rather than per person, according to [Istanbul Tours by Locals](https://www.istanbultoursbylocals.com/blog/tipping-in-turkey/). Adjust upward for larger family groups of six or more.

Always hand tips to your guide and driver in separate envelopes—or separately in person—at the end of your final day together so there is no ambiguity over how the sum is split. On large shared group tours (15+ passengers), 200–400 TL per person for the guide and half that for the driver is standard. Never feel pressured to tip a guide who pushes unrequested carpet, leather, or jewelry shop stops; genuine client-first guides earn their rate through historical depth and logistics, not retail commissions.
Do you tip hamam attendants and hotel porters in TL or EUR?

Tip hamam attendants and hotel porters in Turkish lira whenever possible. While guides and private drivers can easily spend or change crisp euro or dollar banknotes, hotel bellhops, housekeepers, and bathhouse staff lose time and exchange margins converting small foreign bills—and foreign coins are effectively unexchangeable at Turkish banks, as noted in [Clever Tourists' 2026 tipping guide](https://clevertourists.com/resources/tipping-in-turkey-istanbul-restaurants-lira-guide).
Keep these practical habits in mind for cash gratuities:

items: Traditional Hamams: Tip your tellak (male attendant) or natır (female attendant) 10%–20% of the scrub-and-foam package price in cash TL right after your treatment. Historic luxury bathhouses sometimes collect pooled tips at reception—ask when checking in.
Hotel Porters & Bellhops: 50–100 TL per bag (or 100–200 TL for a full luggage cart) handed directly when bags reach your room.
Housekeeping: 100–200 TL per night left daily on the bedside table rather than in one lump sum at checkout, since shift rotations change daily.

Taxis: Locals do not tip percentage rates on cabs; simply round up a fair metered fare to the nearest 50 TL (see our [Istanbul taxi tips and scam guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/istanbul-taxi-tips-scams)).

body.text: When is a service charge already included on the bill?

Under a landmark amendment to the Price Tag Regulation published in Türkiye's Official Gazette on January 30, 2026, restaurants, cafés, and patisseries are legally prohibited from adding mandatory service charges (servis ücreti), cover charges (kuver), or table fees to your bill. Any gratuity you leave is now 100% voluntary, per the [Turkish Ministry of Trade announcement](https://ticaret.gov.tr/haberler/ticaret-bakanligi-tarafindan-fiyat-etiketi-yonetmeliginde-degisiklik-yapildi).

As summarized in [LBF Partners' legal brief on the January 2026 regulation](https://www.lbfpartners.com/en/news/new-regulations-in-the-food-and-beverage-services-sector-under-the-regulation-on-price-tags), venues also cannot charge you for unsolicited bread, water, or starters brought to the table before you order. If a tourist-zone restaurant still prints a Servis %10 or Kuver line on your receipt (adisyon), politely point it out and ask for an itemized fiscal receipt (mali fiş) reflecting only what you ordered—and do not add an extra tip on top if an unauthorized fee was already collected.

faq.q: Is it rude not to tip in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Tipping in Türkiye is genuinely discretionary. Unlike the United States, hospitality workers are not paid sub-minimum tipped wages, so skipping a tip after poor or dishonest service is completely acceptable.

faq.q: Can I add a tip to my credit card at Turkish restaurants?
faq.a: Usually not, and even when a terminal allows it, card tips are often taxed as venue revenue rather than going straight to your waiter. Keep small Turkish lira banknotes on hand for tips.

faq.q: Are foreign coins accepted as tips in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Turkish banks and exchange offices (döviz) do not accept foreign coins. Leaving €2 coins or US quarters creates unusable clutter for staff—always tip in Turkish lira notes.

faq.q: How much should I tip my Cappadocia hot air balloon pilot?
faq.a: Balloon pilots are not routinely tipped, though passengers occasionally leave 200–500 TL per couple in the ground crew's tip box after a smooth landing and champagne toast.

faq.q: What should I do if a restaurant still charges a mandatory kuver or service fee in 2026?
faq.a: Politely remind the server that mandatory kuver and servis ücreti fees were banned on January 30, 2026, request a corrected official fiscal receipt, and avoid double-tipping.

faq.q: Should I tip my airport transfer driver?
faq.a: For a punctual private airport transfer with luggage assistance, 150–300 TL (around €3–€6) per vehicle is appreciated, though never obligatory.
